questions.stem: What is local anaesthesia in contrast to regional anaesthesia?
questions.answer: Local anaesthetic infiltrated directly around the operative site

questions.stem: Regional anaesthesia types include central neuraxial blockade, peripheral nerve blockade and ____ regional anaesthesia.
Besides local anaesthetics, which drugs are used intrathecally and epidurally in regional anaesthesia?
Which drugs are adjuncts used with local anaesthetics in regional anaesthesia?
What stress response to surgery does regional anaesthesia reduce?
Which two outcomes are controversially claimed to improve with regional anaesthesia over general anaesthesia?
questions.answer: Fewer surgical site infections and less cancer recurrence

questions.stem: Which procedure is a reason to use regional anaesthesia for awake neurological monitoring?
What advantage does regional anaesthesia have in obstetrics?
Which is a contraindication to any regional anaesthesia?
What local problem at the needle site contraindicates regional anaesthesia?
questions.answer: Local infection at the puncture site

questions.stem: Which allergy is a contraindication to regional anaesthesia?
Coagulopathy is a contraindication, but less strictly so for which blocks?
What are two contraindications to peripheral nerve blockade?
questions.answer: Pre-existing neuropathy, or need for neurological monitoring

questions.stem: Which condition is a contraindication specific to neuraxial blockade?
Which block-specific risks apply to an interscalene block?
Which two drug classes must be checked for cessation before regional anaesthesia?
What must be covered when consenting a patient for regional anaesthesia?
questions.answer: Risks and complications, respecting patient autonomy
